preservation_map.claim: ## Scope and main contribution
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ## Interaction analytics
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Portal analytics collect user activity for CPO review of business product usage. The required PROD retention period is three months. Permitted fields, the full set of authorized readers, handling of identifiable values, and the retention clock and expiry treatment remain open. [Analytics purpose](../../../records/candidates/observability/KT-observability-and-performance.md#interaction-purpose-and-event-vocabulary) · [Retention criterion](../../../records/candidates/observability/KT-observability-and-performance.md#portal-analytics-ac-001)
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim:
- The analytics effort aims to understand user interaction, improve adoption, and reduce time to value.
- Captured UI elements include tiles, modals, workspace tabs, buttons, switches, and dropdowns.
- Tiles and modals expose open and close events; tabs, buttons, and switches expose click events; dropdowns expose select events.
- Event identity combines container, tile, and component name. Optional values and custom attributes describe interactions such as searches, but do not define an approved vocabulary for every tenant event.
- The example `useAnalytics` hook posts to `/analytics/v1/fmo/print?extend=false`, while the surrounding prose gives `/api/analytics/v1/fmo/print?extend=false` as the requested API. The example uses session-derived authorization and describes deriving client addresses from request headers and the remote address. No credentials, tokens, or individual user data are reproduced.
- `AnalyticsData` declares 20 custom attribute fields, while `AnalyticsType` declares 10. The supported producer, transport, and storage limit remains unresolved.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: Related concept: [[concepts/interaction-analytics]]. Governance concern: telemetry governance.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: ## Usage dashboards
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The [[entities/kibana]] dashboard guide reports nine dashboards for Portal usage: authentication, authentication errors, tiles, workspace movement, workspace additions, selected buttons, login choices, and themes. The error dashboard exposes `traceId` for investigation, and the guide describes downloadable raw data. Its Production dashboard URL remains a placeholder. These statements do not prove present dashboard availability or data completeness.

preservation_map.claim: ## Frontend performance and non-functional requirements
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The current candidate sets a five-second API loading limit. The clarification specifies no mandatory UI performance metric. API scope, timing boundaries, workload, environment, and measurement method remain open. [API loading limit](../../../records/candidates/observability/KT-observability-and-performance.md#current-api-loading-limit) · [API performance criterion](../../../records/candidates/observability/KT-observability-and-performance.md#portal-api-perf-ac-001)
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The monitoring page proposes weekly review of development performance. It discusses login, post-login, and blotter rendering with cache and compression changes.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The May 2023 performance document is explicitly a draft. Its sign-off table has no attached approval or sign-off date. It lists draft targets of five-second response time, 100 users, CPU below 50 percent, and JavaScript heap below 80 percent. Its scenarios cover login, home, trade, cashflow, exception, and rules pages. Its tools include browser performance monitoring and Lighthouse. The plan assumes supporting APIs remain available and sufficiently responsive.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The draft reports login FCP 0.8 seconds and LCP 1.3 seconds, plus home FCP 0.9 seconds and LCP 1.3 seconds. The underlying screenshots and measurement captures are absent from the supplied copy. These values cannot establish present performance or capacity, and the draft targets are not approved current service limits.

preservation_map.claim: ## Cache strategy and update limits
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The cache guide proposes revalidation of layer entry files and longer caching of subsequent static files. Its table assigns 120 days to chunks, images, CSS, fonts, JSON, and icons. A changed entry should reference new subsequent files under the described approach. Users still need logout or page refresh to obtain updated UI code, and the guide explicitly excludes a first-load improvement. These are documented design rules; current response headers and build naming remain unverified. The cache implementation section contains no configuration.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.
